thread:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: multiple 503s from kv-cache in us-west-2 (region). Affected routes: /v1/generate (p95 latency up). Linking incident: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-134.

incident-bot: Page triggered at 2026-07-12T14:18:10Z, page severity: P1. Symptoms: eviction storms, flux in active shards, autoscaler thrash.

Emma (primary): taking this. quick check — are we seeing node flaps or a sudden traffic pattern?

Raj (secondary): I see increased eviction metrics across caches: kv_evictions/s spiking from 30 -> 120 in last 3m. CPU on a subset of pods at 95%. not a network issue.

Oliver SRE: checking node kubelet logs now. If pods are getting OOMKilled or evicted due to memory, we need to adjust eviction thresholds.

Kia Support: FYI a handful of customer chats reporting "service unavailable" errors when calling embeddings endpoint. Customers: acme-corp, finlytics.

Emma (primary): good to know. immediate mitigation plan: 1) scale up dedicated kv-cache pool 2) shift traffic off us-west-2 to us-west-1 for high-risk routes 3) enable aggressive prefix caching for common prompts.

Raj (secondary): I'm on scale-up. Running: ```kubectl scale deployment kv-cache --replicas=12 -n rw-infra-uswest2``` will post output.

deploy-bot: deploy started: scale kv-cache -> 12 replicas (request by Raj). CI checks passed.

Raj (secondary): scaled, new pods pending. Not all nodes have spare GPU memory, scheduling backoff for 2 pods.

Oliver SRE: scheduling backoff likely due to node allocatable memory pressure. Running quick drain of three low-priority pods to free up memory: ```for p in $(kubectl get pods -n rw-infra-uswest2 -o name | grep lowprio); do kubectl delete $p -n rw-infra-uswest2; done```

Emma (primary): while Oliver frees nodes, I'll start traffic steering. Using routing console to set policy: route /v1/generate pref=us-west-1, fallback=us-west-2, weight=80/20. Link: https://console.redwood/routing

Kia Support: routing change noted. customer-facing messages queued: "We are mitigating a transient service disruption in us-west. If you continue to see issues, please ping support."

incident-bot: mitigation step completed: routing adjustment applied by Emma. Autoscaler reports a spike; watch p95.

Raj (secondary): pods started and became ready. p95 for generate dropped from 620ms -> 210ms in us-west-1. us-west-2 still shows errors but decreasing.

Oliver SRE: found repeated oom_kill logs on kv-worker-7 and kv-worker-9. Crash loop due to cache compaction bug after recent config tweak. Patch queued: revert config change in next minute.

Emma (primary): revert config now (rollback configmap kv-compact-config to v2.1). Command: ```kubectl rollout restart daemonset/kv-worker -n rw-infra-uswest2 && kubectl apply -f configmaps/kv-compact-config-v2.1.yaml -n rw-infra-uswest2```

deploy-bot: rollback applied, daemonset restart in progress.

Oliver SRE: daemonset restart completed, no new OOMs. Eviction rate trending down.

Raj (secondary): ingress 503s reduced by ~90% in the last 8m. customers restored.

Kia Support: chasing up acme-corp and finlytics — both confirmed service is back to normal. Logged with CSAT note.

Emma (primary): quick summary for handoff:
- Incident: KV-cache eviction spike in us-west-2 triggered P1 page. Root cause: recent cache compaction config change + memory pressure causing OOMs and evictions.
- Mitigations performed: scaled kv-cache pool, drained low-priority pods, traffic steering to us-west-1, rolled back config, restarted kv-worker daemonset.
- Current status: traffic routing set to 80/20 (us-west-1/us-west-2). Evictions returned to baseline. No active 503s reported.
- Customer impact: short (~12m) elevated 503s for /v1/generate for a subset of users; major customers validated restored.
- Metrics to watch: kv_evictions/s, p95 latency /v1/generate, node allocatable memory, pod OOM events.

Emma (primary): action items / next steps:
- Oliver: follow up with infra team to investigate why compaction config caused OOMs (postmortem item). Link runbook: https://confluence.redwood/runbooks/kv-eviction.
- Raj: keep autoscaler tuned; set a guard to prevent scale-down below 8 replicas during compaction window.
- Kia: follow up with CS on affected customers and add incident note.
- On-call next shift: keep routing weight at 80/20 until 2h after last observed eviction.

Oliver SRE: will open a Jira (INFRA-2178) and start root cause analysis, collecting heap profiles and compaction logs.

Raj (secondary): set autoscaler guard: ```kubectl patch hpa kv-cache -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":8}}' -n rw-infra-uswest2``` applied.

Kia Support: customer notes updated, CS will send one summary email to affected customers later today.

Emma (primary): handoff to night shift: I'm logging detailed runbook steps in the incident page. If you see eviction rate > 10/s or new OOMs, escalate to paging P1 again. Primary for the next shift: @Raj (you'll be primary during UTC night). Secondary: @Oliver SRE.

Raj (secondary): acknowledged, I'll own the night and monitor dashboards for 2h.

Oliver SRE: ack, will collect artifacts and leave instructions in the incident page for reruns and debug commands.

incident-bot: incident INC-2026-134 status updated to "stabilized" (P1 -> P0). Timeline and actions recorded.

Emma (primary): final note — update runbook to include this config compaction caveat and add a short test in staging to exercise compaction at scale. I'll create a PR for the runbook tomorrow. :memo:

Raj (secondary): thanks all. Passing handoff at 2026-07-12T16:13:10Z.

Kia Support: leaving a short public status update for customers in 15m.

Emma (primary): closing thread for now. if anything else flares, poke the channel or page oncall. :thumbsup:
